claim: Tensor parallelism costs 8Bbsh communication volume per transformer block (four all-reduces across forward and backward), whereas a PP+FSDP schedule costs 36Bh^2/U per iteration.
stance_target: the claim that TP is the most communication-expensive topology per unit of compute, and that a TP-free PP+FSDP recipe is cheaper on a bandwidth-limited fabric
scope_conditions: Transformer block with hidden size h; B micro-batches per device, micro-batch size b, sequence length s; U micro-batches per scheduling unit; ~12h^2 parameters per block
quoted_support: In terms of 3D parallelism, TP requires four all-reduce operations during the forward pass and backward pass, resulting in a communication volume of 8Bbsh in a transformer block ... we can calculate the total communication volume in one iteration as 36Bh2/U.

claim: ZeroPP's PP+ZeRO-3 recipe has lower communication volume than TP-based 3D parallelism whenever 2sUb > 9h, a condition easily met at long sequence lengths and large batches.
stance_target: the claim that at 32k training context and large global batches, dropping TP in favour of PP+FSDP is the right call on a slow fabric
scope_conditions: Transformer block, sequence length s, micro-batch b, U micro-batches per scheduling unit, hidden size h
quoted_support: Therefore, as long as the condition 2sUb > 9h is satisfied, the communication volume of ZeroPP introduced by intra-operator parallelism is smaller than that of conventional 3D parallelism. Current models prefer to have larger sequence lengths and are trained with larger batch sizes, which makes the condition quite easy to meet in practice

claim: On an 8-GPU 6.2B GPT microbenchmark, ZeRO-3 has lower communication volume and shorter iteration time than TP at every global batch size tested, with the gap widening as batch grows.
stance_target: the claim that TP's disadvantage is structural, not a tuning artifact
scope_conditions: 6.2B GPT, 8 GPUs, varying global batch size
quoted_support: We test the 6.2B GPT model parallelized with the two methods, respectively, across 8 GPUs with varying global batch sizes, and estimate the per-GPU communication volume for each method. Consequently, ZeRO-3 gains superior communication efficiency, and the performance gap becomes more pronounced as the global batch size increases.

claim: ZeroPP achieves up to 33% higher throughput than conventional 3D parallelism at comparable GPU memory consumption.
stance_target: the expected size of the win from replacing TP with PP+FSDP
scope_conditions: Up to 64 A800-80GB GPUs across 8 InfiniBand nodes; GPT models
quoted_support: we demonstrate that ZeroPP achieves significant performance gains of up to 33% compared to conventional 3D parallelism while maintaining comparable GPU memory consumption.

claim: TP is typically performed across GPUs within a node because it needs high bandwidth, and it requires intrusive modification of single-GPU model code.
stance_target: the claim that TP has no viable home on a box whose fastest link is PCIe Gen2 x4
quoted_support: TP is typically performed across GPUs within a node with high bandwidth. Moreover, implementing TP requires intricate modification to the single GPU code and poses a substantial burden on data scientists and AI practitioners

claim: TP communication is hard to overlap with computation because of strong intra-block data dependencies, whereas FSDP-style communication can be overlapped by layerwise prefetching.
stance_target: the claim that FSDP/DDP hide latency better than TP on a slow fabric
scope_conditions: Transformer blocks under TP vs PP+ZeRO-3
quoted_support: Firstly, the communication in TP is challenging to overlap with computation due to the strong intra-block data dependency, whereas the communication in ZeroPP can be easily overlapped by layerwise data prefetching

claim: A 14.6B model trained on 32 A800 GPUs with PP=4 and global batch 192 shows ZeroPP's advantage over 3D parallelism growing as the memory limit tightens.
stance_target: the claim that PP+FSDP is the better choice when per-card memory is the binding constraint (as on 64 GB cards)
scope_conditions: 14.6B model, 32 A800-80GB GPUs, PP size 4, global batch 192
quoted_support: We conduct experiments using a 14.6B model on 4-node A800 machines with 32 GPUs ... The PP size is uniformly set to 4 and the global batch size is fixed to 192 ... as the memory limitation becomes more stringent, the advantage of ZeroPP becomes increasingly evident.

claim: ZeRO-3 keeps communication volume identical to vanilla DP at stage 1 and remains more communication-efficient than TP at stage 3.
stance_target: the claim that FSDP is the cheapest way to get memory savings without paying TP's communication bill
quoted_support: ZeRO stage 1 (ZeRO-1) solely partitions the optimizer states, exhibiting consistent communication volume compared to vanilla DP. ZeRO stage 3 (ZeRO-3) partitions the optimizer states, gradients, and parameters, and requires extra parameter gathering before each forward and backward computation. But ZeRO-3 remains more communication-efficient than TP.

claim: Naively combining ZeRO-3 with PP causes repeated parameter gathering and gradient synchronization per micro-batch, which is why a specialized breadth-first pipeline schedule is required.
stance_target: the caveat that PP+FSDP composition is not free and needs a schedule that amortizes unsharding across micro-batches
scope_conditions: ZeRO-3 + PP with frequent micro-batch switches
quoted_support: the combination of ZeRO-3 and PP as a hybrid parallelism method entails significant repetitive parameter gathering and gradient synchronization due to frequent micro-batch computation switches in PP. The high-frequency communication results in poor efficiency.
